## The claim

P4-23: chloroquine and the other D2 stress drugs are more potent in high-aneuploidy cell lines than in low-aneuploidy ones

**Prediction if true.** across PRISM lines split by published aneuploidy score, chloroquine shows greater potency in the high-aneuploidy group (one-sided rank test p < 0.05), and most D2 drugs point the same way

**What would refute it.** chloroquine shows no aneuploidy trend at p < 0.2, or the high-aneuploidy group is less sensitive

| 205 | refutes | 0.60 | measurement | Chloroquine shows no aneuploidy selectivity in PRISM (Cliff's δ +0.027, 95 % CI −0.088–0.142, n 241 high vs 180 low, one-sided p 0.315); the tertile split gives p 0.372 and chloroquine is absent from the 20Q2 dose-response release. | `docs/iteration4/step-9/methodology/151-prism-replication-of-the-track2-leads.md` |
| 206 | neutral | 0.30 | measurement | Three of four D2 drugs (bortezomib, metformin, chloroquine) still point toward high-aneuploidy lines being more sensitive, none reaching p < 0.05, so the screen withholds support rather than reversing the direction. | `docs/iteration4/step-9/methodology/151-prism-replication-of-the-track2-leads.md` |
